quoted_clause: GPU memory utilization per request (derived from NVIDIA management library stats)
observed: NVML reports device-level memory usage, not per-request attribution. Per-request memory requires allocator/request instrumentation.
correction: Change to 'device-level GPU memory utilization from NVML, plus allocator/request-level instrumentation for per-request attribution'.
acceptance_test: The text no longer claims NVML alone yields per-request GPU memory.
verdict_evidence: chapter-25/chapter-25.md §25.4 lists 'GPU memory utilization per request (derived from NVIDIA management library stats)'; NVML exposes device-level memory counters only, with no per-request attribution, so the sentence credits NVML with a quantity it cannot produce.
fix_instruction: Change the bullet to 'device-level GPU memory utilization (NVML) plus allocator/request-level instrumentation for per-request attribution'.

page_hint: Ch 25 §7 What We Still Don't Know, Tooling gaps
quoted_clause: Tooling gaps: [1P][FACT] — no widely adopted tool exists for ADR graph visualization or impact analysis (a factual tooling observation, not an open hypothesis)
observed: The claim is a market/tooling observation, not a first-party specification or primary-source fact. Labeling it [1P][FACT] overstates the evidence class and is time-sensitive.
correction: Change to '[2°][FACT] as of this writing' or '[HYPOTHESIS]' and add a date/scope, e.g., 'no widely adopted tool was identified as of the evidence cutoff'.
acceptance_test: The label matches the provenance of the claim and the statement is dated or scoped so it does not read as a permanent first-party fact.
verdict_evidence: ch25 l.264 heads the bullet 'Fleet-level effect' but only re-screens KV (344/35.0 = 9.8 -> ceil 10, +1 = 11), while the same mini-case (l.266: 'already needs 21 hosts on the KV screen (22 under the case (ii) prefill screen)') and ch24 l.99-102 put the peak prefill screen at 19 (case i) / 22 (case ii), which a ~11-host fleet violates; the ADR also never answers the case question posed at l.253.
fix_instruction: Rewrite ch25 l.264: 'the peak KV-residency screen moves from 21 hosts to ~11 (ceil(344/35.0)+1); the fleet remains bounded by the prefill screen - 19 hosts under case (i), 22 under case (ii)', and add an explicit 'Case affected: (i) only' line as l.253 asks.

quoted_clause: This ~30 GB is a *per-request working-set* figure for this ADR's single-request arithmetic; it is **not a re-labeling of** the ~64 GB runtime/workspace/NCCL reserve the body uses elsewhere (140 GB weights + ~436 GB KV budget + ~64 GB reserve = the 640 GB HBM envelope), and this ADR's single-request ~170 GB footprint is not an envelope term. The two answer different questions — one sizes a single request's working set, the other reserves headroom for the serving stack's runtime — and at serving time the ~6 GB transient working set is drawn from *within* that 64 GB workspace line (workspace includes activation buffers) — that ~6 GB is a transient single-request prefill peak, reused across the batch rather than held per request in flight (17 concurrent × 6 GB is not implied), while the 24.1 GB KV is held per request in flight — so the envelope closes as 140 + 436 + 64 = 640, not 670.
observed: This is an extremely dense passage: two long sentences containing at least six parenthetical clarifications, four em-dashes, and the envelope equation, all compressed into a single paragraph. The distinction it draws (single-request working set vs. envelope term) is important and correct, but the delivery makes it very hard to follow on first read.
correction: Break into shorter sentences or a small two-row table: Row 1 = single-request working set (140 GB weights + 24.1 GB KV + ~6 GB transient ≈ 170 GB); Row 2 = serving envelope (140 GB weights + 436 GB KV budget + 64 GB reserve = 640 GB). Then state in one sentence why the 30 GB is not an envelope term (the ~6 GB transient is drawn from within the 64 GB reserve; the 24.1 GB KV is subsumed by the 436 GB budget at concurrency).
acceptance_test: A reader can identify the two distinct quantities (working set vs. envelope) and the envelope equation in a single pass without re-reading.
verdict_evidence: ch25 l.253 ('The concurrency ceiling is now limiting throughput below the target request rate') and l.259 ('To reach the target request rate we need either more host capacity or more KV residency per host') contradict the book's own screen: 21 hosts x 17.5 = 367.5 >= 344 in-flight, and l.266 itself says the canonical peak 'already needs 21 hosts on the KV screen'.
fix_instruction: Restate the premise at ch25 l.253/259 as a per-host constraint (17.5 concurrent/host vs 344 fleet in-flight, met at 21 hosts = 367.5), and delete the claim that the target rate is currently unreachable, or state the current under-provisioned fleet size.

observed: The opening describes the deployment as FP16, but ADR 0016 in the same chapter has Status: Accepted and its Consequences state "this record sets the canonical deployment's precision label to BF16." If the ADR is accepted, the current state should be BF16.
correction: Either change the opening to "a 70B dense BF16 deployment" (reflecting the accepted ADR) or add a clarifying clause such as "a 70B dense FP16 deployment — the state that ADR 0016 in this chapter will change to BF16."
acceptance_test: The opening paragraph and ADR 0016's Accepted status describe the same temporal state, or the temporal relationship is explicitly stated.
verdict_evidence: ch25:5 'FP16 deployment' vs ADR 0016 BF16 accepted (ch25:36-56); ch26:57 carries house fix.
fix_instruction: Add '(FP16 label; see ADR 0016)' after '70B dense FP16 deployment'.

quoted_clause: The format was popularized by Michael Nygard
observed: The attribution to Michael Nygard is correct but lacks a citation.
correction: Add a citation to Nygard's original blog post or a standard ADR reference in the references section.
acceptance_test: The attribution includes a verifiable reference.
verdict_evidence: §1 L11 and the template L79 enumerate only proposed/accepted/superseded/deprecated, yet ADR 0015 L192 sets '**Status:** **HOLD**' and L186 calls writing HOLD 'the correct, auditable record'.
fix_instruction: Add 'hold' to the §1 status list and to the template's Status line (e.g. '<proposed | accepted | hold | superseded | deprecated>') so the copy-ready template can record the state the chapter endorses.

quoted_clause: For a team of ~10 engineers making ~1–2 significant architectural decisions per month, this is a manageable cost. The payoff — reduced on-call noise, faster onboarding, and fewer "why did we do it this way?" debates — is expected to compensate.
observed: The "~10 engineers" and "~1–2 decisions per month" figures are illustrative assumptions, and "is expected to compensate" is a prediction. Neither carries an evidence label.
correction: Tag the cost figures as [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] and the payoff claim as [HYPOTHESIS], consistent with the tagging discipline the chapter itself advocates.
acceptance_test: All empirical or predictive claims in §25.6 carry evidence labels from the book's taxonomy.
verdict_evidence: Fig 25.1 (chapter-25/chapter-25.md:182) says the record is 'kept, not edited', while :168 instructs 'If a decision is superseded, update the ADR status and add a superseding ADR link' and :237 says a successor supersedes ADR 0015 while it 'stays on file unchanged'. Status metadata is a field that must change on supersession.
fix_instruction: At chapter-25/chapter-25.md:182 change 'it is kept, not edited' to 'its decision body is kept, not rewritten (status is updated to superseded, with a link to the successor)', and align :237's 'unchanged' to 'decision body unchanged'.

quoted_clause: per-request KV at 9.2K = 24.1 GB ... at concurrency the 9.5K-maximum per-request figure applies (17 × ~24.9 GB ≈ 423 GB)
observed: The paragraph uses two different context lengths (9.2K → 24.1 GB and 9.5K → 24.9 GB) in the same dense passage. The switch is called out but adds to the paragraph's already high cognitive load (see CH25-02).
correction: If CH25-02's restructuring is adopted, separate the single-request working set (9.2K) from the concurrency analysis (9.5K) into distinct sentences or table rows, making the context-length switch immediately visible.
acceptance_test: The reader can immediately identify which context length applies to which figure without re-reading.
verdict_evidence: L195 prints '10 rps average x 8 h x 260 workdays' with no 3,600 s/h and no /12; 10*8*3600*260 = 74,880,000 (12x the printed 6.24M), while Ch 16 L90 and Ch 22 L117 carry the full 'x 3,600 s/h x 260 workdays / 12 = 6,240,000'.
fix_instruction: Restore the missing factors in ADR 0015's Context parenthetical: '10 rps average x 8 h x 3,600 s/h x 260 workdays / 12 = 6.24M requests/mo' (matching Ch 16 L90); keep the '~2.4 rps monthly denominator' clause, which is correct.

page_hint: Fig 25.1 caption (Ch 25 §6) vs Ch 25 §1 and Table 25-1
quoted_clause: an ADR is a fixed five-field record — Title & status, Context (the situation), Decision (the choice), Consequences (the effects), Alternatives (the rejected options) — and it is *kept, not edited*
observed: 'Kept, not edited' contradicts the chapter's own status-tracking practice. §1 says ADRs are 'living, reviewed in pull requests'; Table 25-1's fix for 'No status tracking' is to 'update the ADR status and add a superseding ADR link'; and the ADR 0015 falsification path says a successor 'lifts the HOLD and supersedes this one' — a status edit.
correction: Rewrite as: 'and it is *kept, not rewritten*: the reasoning of a superseded ADR is preserved verbatim, while only its status, supersession link and review date are updated.'
acceptance_test: The figure caption and Table 25-1 can be read together without contradiction; the caption explicitly permits status/supersession updates.
verdict_evidence: Fig 25.1 caption L182 says the record is '*kept, not edited*', but §1 L19 calls ADRs 'living, reviewed in pull requests' and Table 25-1 L168 instructs 'update the ADR status and add a superseding ADR link' — a status edit.
fix_instruction: Qualify the caption: 'kept on file — the body is never rewritten; only the Status line is updated when a successor supersedes it.'

quoted_clause: so 'adding a second host' misunderstands the scale
observed: The phrase "adding a second host" is confusing because the fleet already has 21 hosts. "A second host" implies going from 1 to 2, not from 21 to 22.
correction: Rephrase to "just add another host" or "adding hosts one at a time" to clarify that the objection is about incremental additions not addressing the fleet-scale constraint.
acceptance_test: The phrasing clearly conveys that adding one host does not address the fleet-scale constraint (21+ hosts).
verdict_evidence: L246 tags 'no widely adopted tool exists for ADR graph visualization' [1P][FACT] with no source and no date, but Ch 4 Note 1 (L130) defines [1P] as a first-party *published* source (spec, paper, project artifact) — no such source can attest a universal absence.
fix_instruction: Relabel the tooling-gaps bullet as an open item ([HYPOTHESIS] or [UNRESOLVED]) and date the observation, e.g. 'as of 2026, no widely adopted tool … (author survey, no instrumented source)'.

quoted_clause: The fleet runs a 70-billion-parameter dense model for RAG Q&A serving on an 8×H100 host (640 GB). ... The fleet serves the canonical RAG Q&A workload on an 8×H100 host.
observed: Both passages describe 'the fleet' as a single 8×H100 host, while the canonical fleet in the same chapter is 21 hosts (32 under the N−1 policy). The per-host figure is being used with fleet-level nouns.
correction: Rewrite as 'serving on 8×H100 hosts (640 GB of HBM per host; the canonical fleet is 21 hosts — see ADR 0015 R1)' in §3, and 'on 8×H100 hosts' in the mini-case scenario.
acceptance_test: No sentence in Ch 25 uses 'the fleet' to denote a single host.
verdict_evidence: L42 'The fleet runs a 70-billion-parameter dense model … on an 8xH100 host' and L253 'The fleet serves the canonical RAG Q&A workload on an 8xH100 host' use a single-host scope with fleet-level subjects, while the same chapter sizes 21 hosts (32 under N-1).
fix_instruction: Rewrite both openings at host scope — 'Each serving host in the fleet runs …' / 'The fleet serves the workload on 8xH100 hosts' — leaving the 21/32-host screens unchanged.

page_hint: Ch 25 §3.1 (template, '## Evidence' block) and §4 (final paragraph of Measurement)
quoted_clause:
- <claim> — FACT/DERIVED/HYPOTHESIS
  [1P]/[2°]/(to be verified) ... Each derived quantity should be tagged with its evidence source [1P]/[2°]/(to be verified)
observed: '(to be verified)' is used as if it were a member of the book's evidence-label vocabulary, but the vocabulary defined in Ch 4 / Appendix A uses [UNRESOLVED] on the status axis. The template therefore teaches a label the book does not define, and the §4 sentence mixes a placeholder with two defined provenance labels.
correction: In the template, write '[1P]/[2°]/[LAB] + status: FACT/DERIVED/ASSUMPTION/HYPOTHESIS/UNRESOLVED' and, in §4, replace '(to be verified)' with '[UNRESOLVED]'.
acceptance_test: Every label string that appears in Ch 25 is a member of the Ch 4 / Appendix A vocabulary.
verdict_evidence: The template L100 and §4 L153 place '(to be verified)' in the provenance slot; Ch 4 Note 1 (L130) defines Axis 1 as [1P]/[canonical scenario]/[ILLUSTRATIVE]/[2(deg)]/[LAB] and Axis 2 as FACT/DERIVED/ASSUMPTION/HYPOTHESIS/[UNRESOLVED] — '(to be verified)' occurs only these 2 times in the whole manuscript.
fix_instruction: Replace '(to be verified)' with the defined status token '[UNRESOLVED]' in both the template Evidence block (L100) and the §4 sentence (L153).
